A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SubgraphRAG work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval-recall and timing measurements, question-answering results, ablations, generalization experiments and truth-grounding analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and reports additional baseline comparisons, transfer results and retrieval-budget experiments.

M1.justification: The shortest-path weak supervision, factorized triple scoring, DDE, text-embedding MLP, top-K retrieval and prompting of unfine-tuned LLMs remain unchanged. The added DDE illustration and abbreviated displayed prompt do not establish procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Freebase-based KGQA on WebQSP, CWQ and their answer-present subsets, including cross-dataset transfer. The additional comparisons use these existing datasets and task conditions.

E2.justification: V3 adds SR+NSM w E2E and GNN-RAG to retrieval comparisons, and UniKGQA, SR+NSM w E2E and GNN-RAG to Table 3. GNN-RAG also enters the retriever-swap comparisons in Tables 6 and 9. The retrieval-size plots additionally include cosine similarity. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: The new RoG experiment varies beam-search sizes over 3, 6, 9 and 12 while using SubgraphRAG's reasoners (Figure 7). Tables 3–4 extend the existing transfer protocol to GPT-4o with 100 and 500 triples. Existing metrics, benchmark settings and default retrieval budget remain unchanged; exact GPT model identifiers are newly disclosed.

E4.justification: V3 adds a RoG beam-width sensitivity test, expands retriever-swap and transfer analyses with GNN-RAG, and reports a within-CWQ answer-overlap diagnostic. Retrieved triples make several existing response examples more inspectable. Figure 4 removes the oracle upper-bound curves. These are targeted changes to an already extensive analysis suite.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seed 0 and temperature 0 for SubgraphRAG's LLM reasoners. Neither reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests; the added results do not introduce a different statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial baseline, transfer and beam-sweep results while retaining the original SubgraphRAG benchmark scores. Table 1 changes cosine similarity's GPT-4o-labeled recall from 0.674 to 0.719 on WebQSP and 0.508 to 0.567 on CWQ, and WebQSP answer recall from 0.707 to 0.708. The truth-grounding table also drops two diagnostic result columns.

T1.justification: The optimization formulation, triple factorization, DDE updates, GraphSAGE equations and Scoreh definition are retained. Equation numbering changes, and the new DDE appendix supplies intuition and an illustration without adding a formal derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contribution and claims: lightweight, flexible retrieval followed by unfine-tuned LLM reasoning, with competitive accuracy, efficiency, generalization and grounding. The additional evidence does not redefine those claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds DDE mechanism explanations, acknowledges embedding precomputation's time-memory trade-off, and tentatively attributes some one-hop weaknesses to repeated training/test answers in CWQ. It removes v1's explicit warning that ToG's Hit calculation may overestimate performance, while retaining the inability-to-reproduce caveat.

D1.justification: V3 adds an implementation link, states that full prediction files are available, specifies exact GPT model versions, and supplies retrieved triples for six existing examples. It also documents the added baselines' implementation sources and reproduction difficulties. The displayed ICL example is shortened with an ellipsis; no underlying prompt change is established.

R1.justification: V3 adds references to ChatKBQA, Interactive-KBQA, ReaRev, Janossy pooling and approximate-nearest-neighbor research. Related work changes SQL to SPARQL and more carefully distinguishes path constraints from iterative retrieval costs. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The introduction, preliminaries, method exposition and experimental discussion undergo widespread condensation and rewriting. V3 removes the short related-work pointer subsection, moves the truth-grounding discussion into the appendix, adds a DDE appendix, and separates successful-response and refusal examples into subsections. This substantially reorganizes the presentation.

P2.justification: V3 adds DDE and RoG beam-sweep figures, expands retrieval-plot legends and comparator displays, and redraws Figure 4 without upper bounds using revised axes. Tables gain rows, the truth-grounding table moves to the appendix and loses columns, and prompt/example panels are abbreviated or expanded and redistributed. These are substantial display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The added neural baselines and RoG budget control strengthen the comparative evidence, while model identifiers and retrieved-example inputs improve inspectability. Benefits are limited by retained overbroad superiority language: v3 Table 6 shows the GNN-RAG swap outperforming SubgraphRAG on CWQ-sub Scoreh. Removing oracle curves and diagnostic columns also reduces some analytical detail. The net gain is useful but limited.
